title: Purchasing information model · Supplier
notes: Context gap: no procedure, form, export, existing catalogue or workflow design was supplied, and no project manifest existed in the working directory. Everything below is a reasoned baseline built from the question itself, not from customer evidence. Confirm it against the real purchasing procedure before configuring anything.

Country is provisional. No country was stated, so Angola is the disclosed starting context (AOA, Africa/Luanda). Currency options, the taxpayer-number field and the address wording change if that is wrong. No Angolan legal requirement is asserted here; nothing in this catalogue is derived from law.

A Provia MCP server is exposed in this session, but the read call (org_get_context) was not authorised, so no destination organization was read. Existing entity types, icons, field types and permission levels in the tenant are unverified. Treat this as disconnected-mode design.

The short answer to the question: Supplier is an entity type; a purchase request is a workflow case, not an entity. The supplier holds what stays true between requests; the request holds what is true of one execution. The case-side field list is in purchase-request-fields.md, which is not part of this catalogue schema.
Icons come from the bundled snapshot, product source revision 36772f7ce0831f0ea6f85a0e3e7849d32e576655. Destination availability is pending verification.
Field types and configuration checked against Provia revision 2641364d9c1aa0aa2b76aa788ef521bcb6218118. This is an editorial specification for manual setup, not a Provia import payload.

Use tags, not fields, for flexible labels the organization wants to change often (for example 'local supplier', 'framework agreement', 'sole source'). Use the select fields below only for vocabularies somebody owns and governs.

types.name: Supplier
types.description: Suppliers selected in purchase requests, contracting and supplier evaluation. Holds the identification, contacts and commercial terms needed to choose the counterparty and act on the relationship.
types.namePattern: Trading name as it appears on the supplier's own invoices; add the existing supplier code in parentheses only when two records would otherwise be indistinguishable.
types.purpose: Selecting the counterparty in a purchase request, comparing quotations, contracting, preparing payment and periodic supplier evaluation.
types.owner: Not established by any supplied source. Proposed: Procurement maintains identification, contacts, classification and status; Finance confirms the taxpayer number and the ERP link. Confirm before setup.

fields.label: Registered name
fields.helpText: Fill in only when the registered name on contracts and invoices differs from the trading name used as the record Name.
fields.purpose: Name the correct legal counterparty on a contract or purchase order when it differs from the trading name.
fields.source: Supplier's own registration documents, collected at registration.
fields.maintainer: Procurement, at registration; reviewed if the supplier notifies a change.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Taxpayer number (NIF)
fields.helpText: The taxpayer number the finance team uses to match this supplier in the accounting system. Confirm which identifier your finance team actually keys on before configuring this field.
fields.purpose: Match the supplier to the accounting record when preparing a purchase order or checking an invoice.
fields.source: Supplier's registration documents; reconciled against the accounting system.
fields.maintainer: Finance confirms the value; Procurement records it at registration.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. Restrict the type to Procurement and Finance rather than granting the whole organization create or edit access; a field-level restriction does not exist.

fields.label: Supplier code in the accounting system
fields.helpText: The code the accounting or ERP system already assigns. Leave empty until that system has created the supplier. Do not invent a code here.
fields.purpose: Reconcile a Provia supplier record with the accounting ledger when a purchase order or invoice is prepared.
fields.source: Accounting or ERP system, which remains authoritative for this value.
fields.maintainer: Finance, after the supplier is created in the accounting system.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Supply category
fields.helpText: What this supplier provides. Configure this field before the sub-category, which depends on it.
fields.purpose: Filter suppliers when a requester looks for a counterparty, and group spending for reporting.
fields.source: Proposed vocabulary; no supplied source establishes the organization's real categories.
fields.maintainer: Procurement owns the vocabulary; changing options requires reviewing existing records and filters.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Supply sub-category
fields.helpText: Only sub-categories belonging to the selected category are offered. Changing the category clears this value.
fields.purpose: Find a qualified supplier for a specific need without reading every record in the category.
fields.source: Illustrative list. Replace with the organization's real sub-categories before setup; these values are a demonstration of the dependent-selection mechanism, not a recommendation.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Criticality if the supplier fails
fields.helpText: How much the operation is disrupted if this supplier stops delivering. Used to decide how often the supplier is re-evaluated and whether an alternative is needed.
fields.purpose: Prioritise supplier evaluation and alternative sourcing.
fields.source: Recommendation. Include only if the organization actually runs a supplier evaluation or sourcing-risk process; otherwise it is a field nobody maintains.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Relationship owner
fields.helpText: Who in the organization answers for this supplier: renegotiation, complaints and evaluation.
fields.purpose: Know who to ask when a request involving this supplier stalls or a delivery problem arises.
fields.source: Proposed; no supplied source names owners.
fields.maintainer: Procurement lead, when the owner changes.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. Selecting a user here does not assign any workflow action to that person.

fields.label: Commercial contact
fields.helpText: The person at the supplier who receives requests for quotation and purchase orders.
fields.purpose: Contact the supplier when a quotation or an order has to be sent.
fields.source: Collected at registration from the supplier.
fields.maintainer: Procurement; corrected whenever a bounced contact is found.
fields.sensitivity: Personal data of a supplier employee. Keep name, business email and business phone only; do not collect personal identity documents here.

fields.label: Commercial email
fields.helpText: Business address used to send requests for quotation and orders.
fields.purpose: Send the request for quotation and the purchase order.
fields.source: Collected at registration from the supplier.
fields.sensitivity: Business contact data. A field here does not trigger any notification; Provia notifications address users and groups, not entity fields.

fields.label: Commercial phone
fields.helpText: Alternative channel when an order or delivery needs urgent coordination.
fields.purpose: Reach the supplier when email is too slow.
fields.source: Collected at registration from the supplier.
fields.sensitivity: Business contact data.

fields.label: Collection or delivery address
fields.helpText: Where goods are collected from or where the service is performed, when that matters to the order.
fields.purpose: Plan collection, delivery or a site visit.
fields.source: Collected at registration; relevant mainly for goods and works suppliers.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Country of establishment
fields.helpText: Fill in for suppliers established outside the country of operation, where import handling and lead time differ.
fields.purpose: Anticipate import handling, longer lead times and a foreign-currency price when planning a request.
fields.source: Collected at registration.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. No customs or tax consequence is asserted here; confirm any such rule with the finance team.

fields.label: Usual invoicing currency
fields.helpText: The currency this supplier normally quotes in. The actual currency of a given request is recorded on the request, not here.
fields.purpose: Warn the requester that a quotation will arrive in foreign currency before the comparison is built.
fields.source: Observed from the supplier's quotations; proposed option list.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Agreed payment term (days)
fields.helpText: Days from invoice to payment as agreed with this supplier. Zero means payment on delivery. This value informs planning; it does not schedule or block a payment.
fields.purpose: Plan the cash impact of a request and check an invoice against the agreed term.
fields.source: Agreement or framework contract with the supplier; unknown for suppliers used ad hoc.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Agreement or price list valid until
fields.helpText: End date of the framework agreement or agreed price list, when one exists. Leave empty for suppliers with no standing agreement.
fields.purpose: Tell the requester whether agreed prices still apply or a fresh quotation is needed.
fields.source: The signed agreement, which remains the authoritative document.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. An expired date does not prevent anyone from selecting the supplier.

fields.label: Supplier status
fields.helpText: Where the supplier stands with the organization today. Check it before selecting a supplier; Provia does not filter or block selection on this value.
fields.purpose: Stop a requester from selecting a supplier that is still being registered or has been suspended.
fields.source: Proposed lifecycle. The real qualification steps are unknown; no supplied source defines them.
fields.maintainer: Procurement, with whoever approves supplier registration.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. A custom status field is a label, not an access or selection control.

fields.label: Registration valid until
fields.helpText: Earliest expiry among the documents your organization requires from a registered supplier. Set it only if a process exists to re-check those documents.
fields.purpose: Trigger a re-check of the supplier's registration before it is used again.
fields.source: Pending. Which documents are required, and whether any requirement is statutory rather than internal policy, is not established by any supplied source and is not asserted here.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. The date does not expire the record or notify anyone by itself.

fields.label: Last evaluation
fields.helpText: Date of the most recent completed supplier evaluation. Leave empty if the supplier has never been evaluated.
fields.purpose: See whether the performance judgement on this supplier is current before awarding again.
fields.source: The evaluation process itself. Drop this field and the next one if no supplier evaluation process exists.
fields.maintainer: Whoever runs the evaluation; entered manually after each one.
fields.sensitivity: Internal.

fields.label: Last evaluation rating
fields.helpText: Result of the evaluation dated above, on a one-to-five scale. The scale's meaning must be defined by the evaluation procedure.
fields.purpose: Compare suppliers when more than one can serve the same need.
fields.source: The evaluation process. A one-to-five scale is a proposal; the real scale is unknown.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. This holds the latest value only; it is not a history of past evaluations.

fields.label: Record in the accounting system
fields.helpText: Link to this supplier in the accounting or ERP system, which stays authoritative for bank details, balances and invoice history.
fields.purpose: Open the financial record without duplicating bank details, balances or invoices in Provia.
fields.source: The accounting or ERP system. Depends on that system having per-supplier addressable pages; unverified.
fields.maintainer: Finance provides the link; Procurement pastes it at registration. No synchronisation exists between the two systems.
fields.sensitivity: Internal. The link exposes whatever the target system's own permissions allow; Provia does not control that.

coverage.reason: Trading name is the native record Name; registered name, taxpayer number and the accounting code cover the cases where the Name is not enough. Category and sub-category support finding a supplier.
One commercial contact with email and phone, plus address and country of establishment where the order depends on them.
A relationship owner is recorded. No parent/subsidiary structure is modelled; nothing in the question suggests group-level purchasing.
One status field covers the whole relationship, with a registration expiry date. Qualification status was deliberately merged into it rather than kept as a second, overlapping status.
Usual currency, agreed payment term and agreement validity are the terms a requester or an approver needs to see before committing. Prices are not held here; they belong to the quotation on the case.

No second entity type is proposed, so there is nothing to link to yet. A link to a Contract or an Item catalogue depends on whether those objects exist and who would maintain them. See the deferred candidates in setup.

Registration documents, quotations, purchase orders and invoices stay with the case that produced them or in the document store. Only the ERP link and the registration expiry date are kept on the supplier.

Account details are the highest-risk data in a purchasing process and have a confirmation procedure of their own in the finance system. Keeping a second copy in Provia creates a fraud surface with no owner. The ERP link covers the lookup need. Revisit only if Provia is meant to prepare payment instructions, which no supplied source says.

setup: No customer evidence was supplied. Every field, option list and owner below is a proposal to confirm against the real purchasing procedure, not a recorded requirement.
Native Name, UUID, creator and system timestamps already exist. No field here duplicates them, and no source_system, source_record_id, verified_at or version field was added.

Configure Supply category before Supply sub-category, then copy each option's parentValue exactly. Do not set a default value on the dependent field. Replace the illustrative sub-categories with the organization's real ones before creating the type; changing them later means reviewing existing records and any filters built on them.

Supplier code is a text field because the accounting system is assumed to assign it. If the organization has no external supplier register, replace it with an auto_number field (required false, no default, prefix SUP-, padding 4, startAt 1) and do not keep both. Automatic numbers can have gaps, are not exported in workflow YAML and cannot be edited once assigned.

Access: this type carries supplier contacts and the taxpayer number. The proposal is create and edit for Procurement and Finance, view for the rest of the organization so requesters can select a supplier. No access grants are declared in this catalogue because no group design exists yet; set them when the groups are defined. Field-level permissions do not exist — the sensitivity notes are guidance, not enforcement.

Deferred entity candidates, with reasons. Purchase request: rejected — it is one execution of a process, so it is a workflow case, not an entity; creating both would duplicate every value and leave two records to keep in step. Quotation: deferred — quotations belong to the request that solicited them; make it an entity only if the same quotation is genuinely reused across requests. Contract or framework agreement: deferred — plausible if contracts have their own renewal and review lifecycle, which no supplied source confirms; today the agreement_valid_until date covers the purchasing need. Item or material catalogue: deferred — worth having only if the organization already maintains a governed item list; otherwise a free-text description on the request is honest. Cost centre or budget line: deferred — belongs to the finance chart of accounts; model it as a select on the case, or as an entity only if finance will maintain it in Provia.
No entity-to-entity relationship is configured, so there is no creation-order dependency. Create Supplier first, then reference it from the purchase request workflow's entity field.

Manual entry walkthrough. Registering 'Demonstration Logistics' from a supplier's own registration pack, a procurement officer knows at creation: trading name (the Name), registered name, taxpayer number, category and sub-category, contact name, email and phone, address, country of establishment and usual currency. Status starts at 'Under registration'. Not known at creation: the accounting code (Finance creates the supplier there afterwards), the ERP link (same), the payment term (agreed later or never, for ad hoc suppliers), agreement validity (only if an agreement is signed), registration expiry (only once someone defines which documents are required) and both evaluation fields (empty until the first evaluation). That is why every field is required false at creation; readiness is checked before award, not at registration.

Unresolved maintenance effort. Three fields have no confirmed owner or update trigger: registration expiry depends on a document re-check process that may not exist; both evaluation fields depend on a supplier evaluation process that may not exist; the accounting code and ERP link depend on Finance doing a second step after registration. If those processes do not exist, remove the fields rather than ship a register that goes stale — a field nobody updates is worse than no field.

The taxpayer number is not verified for uniqueness. Provia does not enforce a uniqueness constraint on a custom field, so two records for the same supplier remain possible; deduplication is a manual search before creating a record.
readiness: Before a purchase request is awarded to this supplier, confirm the status is 'Approved for purchasing', the registration expiry is not past, and the accounting code and ERP link are filled so the order can be placed. None of this is enforced by the fields; make it a check in the award or approval action of the workflow.
Before payment is prepared, confirm the bank details in the finance system, not in Provia. Provia holds no account details by design.
